subject: Hearthline capacity dress rehearsal and go-live window
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@hearthline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hearthline capacity dress rehearsal and go-live window

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Per our conversation, I’m proposing a short staged plan to validate Dedicated capacity sizing and run a production-dress rehearsal prior to an agreed go-live window. The goal is to make the Hosted->Dedicated swap predictable and to validate throughput/SLOs under representative traffic.

High level proposal:
- Week of Aug 2: canary/dress rehearsal (traffic mirror + 1% production shadow / 10% load test during off-peak)
- Aug 9–11: go-live window (final swap with rollback hold-open)

What we need from Hearthline to firm this up:
1) Expected 95th qps and concurrent prompt length distribution (attached sample helps)
2) Any peak timezone(s) to avoid for the canary
3) Procurement PO timing (to schedule reserved capacity reservation)

I attached a quick capacity model (hearthline_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with an initial GPU count and concurrency lanes for A100/RTX-class variants. Ben / Karthik / Monica — can you review the validation criteria and propose a minimal staging checklist (smoke tests, latency percentiles to hit, failure modes)?

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai
redwood.ai
From: Alice Chen <alice@hearthline.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@hearthline.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 11:02:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Hearthline capacity dress rehearsal and go-live window

Hi Vivek —

Thanks, this looks good. Quick answers from our side:
- 95th qps (current peak sustained during business hours): ~420 qps. Spiky bursts up to ~620 qps for short periods (1–3 min).
- Average prompt length is ~1.2k tokens (we’ll share a 24hr sample). Attached: prod-traffic-sample.json.
- Preferred blackout: avoid weekdays 10:00–14:00 PT; off-peak for us is 01:00–05:00 PT.

Procurement is copied; they’ll confirm PO cadence and timeline. We’d like the staging canary the week of Aug 2 if Redwood can stand up the mirrored runs and provide a canary checklist.

Two asks from our security/compliance team:
1) Can you provide an SOC 2 attestation or link to the SOC package for Dedicated?
2) Is there a retention guarantee for logs during the staging period?

Appreciate the clear plan — Alice

--
Alice Chen
VP Product, Hearthline
alice@hearthline.ai
hearthline.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 14:30:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Hearthline capacity dress rehearsal and go-live window

Team —

I reviewed Alice’s numbers and sketched a validation plan. Key points and acceptance criteria:

Staging (canary) scope — week of Aug 2:
- Mirror 1% of live traffic to Dedicated cluster; run synthetic ramp tests to 50/75/100% of expected peak (we should reach 620 qps for 3x sustained and 1.5x spike test).
- Verify 95th latency < 220ms for generation-only paths, p95 end-to-end < 450ms.
- Memory/KV warming test: ensure KV cache hit-rate >= 85% after 30 minutes of mirrored traffic.
- Failure drills: simulate a worker OOM and verify automated fallback to hosted variant with < 30s observed degradation window.

Capacity notes (initial):
- Baseline chosen: 6x A100-40GB equiv nodes with 4 concurrency lanes each; predicted sustained 420 qps with headroom to 600 qps for short bursts. See hearthline_capacity_model_v1.xlsx for reasoning.
- If we see >20% higher observed token-PS, move to 8 nodes and reduce per-instance batch target to keep latency under SLO.

Runbook & artifacts: attached canary-runbook.pdf and qps_projections.xlsx. I added a pre-flight checklist — we should confirm PKI/certs for private endpoint, DocuSign link for the reserved capacity order, and that procurement provides the PO before we reserve capacity.

Proposed calendar:
- Jul 29: internal dry-run (simulate the canary within our staging fleet)
- Aug 2–3: live mirror + synthetic stress during off-peak (01:00–05:00 PT)
- Aug 4: sitrep and go/no-go decision meeting
- Aug 9: start swap window (24–48hr, with immediate rollback plan)

Action items for Karthik/Monica: please finalize autoscaling policies and the traffic ramp script. I’ll own the canary runbook and the rollback play.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:00:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Hearthline capacity dress rehearsal and go-live window

Ben / team —

Quick updates after reviewing the runbook:
- Autoscaling: set target CPU/GPU utilization trigger to 72% with a 90s cooldown. This balances burst headroom with batching efficiency.
- Batch sizing: reduce default batch size from 32 -> 24 for the canary to reduce p95 variance when token lengths spike (Alice’s sample shows higher tail token counts).
- Observability: we’ll add token-level tracing for the first 6 hours of the canary and a synthetic latency probe every 30s. Logs retained for 14 days for this deal (prod default is 7 days) per Alice’s compliance ask.

I attached qps_projections.xlsx with a scenario matrix (low/nominal/high) and the recommended node count per scenario. If canary looks clean at 75% target, we can keep the initial baseline and defer node increase until after 72hrs of observation.

I’ll queue the autoscale policy changes and the traffic ramp job in staging for Jul 29 internal dry-run.

-karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal PM, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Alice Chen <alice@hearthline.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@hearthline.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 16:05:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Hearthline capacity dress rehearsal and go-live window

Hi all —

This looks actionable — Procurement attached a PO stub (Hearthline_PO_7892.pdf). We confirm the Aug 2–3 canary window and Aug 9 as our preferred swap start with an 48hr window for finalization and rollback hold-open.

Security/compliance: we reviewed the SOC2 attestation link you provided (drive link above) and that satisfies the initial ask — we’ll follow up if they need an in-person review. Logs retention at 14 days for the staging period is acceptable.

One final ask: can Redwood include a short, bulletized SLA exception for the swap window in the runbook (what we commit to if the fallback triggers)? If you can add that to the canary-runbook.pdf we’ll be ready to sign the reserved capacity order.

Thanks — looking forward to the rehearsal.

Alice

VP Product, Hearthline
